title: Prevent default Inbox observation from racing explicit project assignment
description: A newly observed session can be published into the local default project while another desktop explicitly assigns the same exact machine/session to its selected project. Verified catalog history contains two concurrent parentless session assignments at the same clock: the observing host chose ungrouped while the launching desktop chose the selected project. A later explicit write merged both parents and restored the intended project. Passive observation must not compete with an explicit launch or move. Preserve deliberate moves to the default project, exact launch/run/session identity, existing conflict review and compatibility with resident clients. Add a synthetic two-peer regression before choosing the protocol or presentation fix.
design: Keep first-observed session rows and their order in the local desktop organization with an unassigned_sessions marker. SwarmController removes those memberships from both initialize and apply payloads; explicit moves and verified launches remove the marker. Shared catalog membership wins over passive placement on refresh, including rename arrival ordering. New payloads carry the additive organization hint session_assignments_explicit so the CLI preserves unseen competing explicit choices instead of applying its legacy passive-observation guard. Older CLIs ignore that hint; shared operation schema, existing assignments/conflicts and unmarked historical caches are unchanged. Full race prevention requires updating observing desktops; the CLI update additionally preserves explicit first-choice conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: A remote session launched into an explicit project remains in that project when another GUI first observes it concurrently; passive fallback display does not create an authoritative competing assignment. Explicit moves to the default project remain synchronized. Existing and real conflicts are preserved for review.
notes:
2026-10-12 validation: the new desktop regression failed before the fix by exporting passive session membership. The fixed source passes all 53 Linux GUI targets and all 15 affected native macOS targets, 27 Swarm unit contracts on Rust 1.85, and 15 isolated real-CLI Swarm tests (14-suite run plus the added compatibility contract). Both observation/launch write orders converge without assignment conflicts; an unseen explicit first choice remains a reviewable conflict. The additive hint also passes against the retained pre-fix CLI binary without changing catalog operations. Source privacy/syntax/version checks and targeted rustfmt pass.
2026-10-12 final integration: the Inbox fix and composer feedback cleanup are reconciled with main 944f19e. Full Linux GUI build and all 53 CTest targets pass; native macOS GUI build and all 15 final integration targets pass, with all 314 staged GUI/build/test source files verified by SHA-256.

title: Remove blocking draft writer barriers from navigation and send UI
description: Review zerus-pta0 against retained 0.41.0 release source: ComposerDraftStore::load and keys call global flushWrites; DraftWrites::flush and sync use BlockingQueuedConnection without a deadline. New-session selection, Saved drafts and explicit sending can therefore block the GUI behind unrelated slow disk writes despite asynchronous typing. A synthetic 400 ms writer delay makes loading an unrelated absent draft block the main thread 410 ms (0.13 ms thread CPU); queued GUI work cannot run. Use asynchronous draft loading and durable-send continuation with operation identity and fresh validation. Preserve atomic persistence before transport, draft recovery and no replay; do not bypass the durable barrier. Test navigation and explicit send while the writer remains stalled. Existing typing responsiveness coverage releases the writer before its send assertion.
design: Use one ordered worker with coalesced edit snapshots and noncoalescing durable operations. All GUI reads/index scans/writes use asynchronous continuations with exact key and revision. Loading may lock only its composer; navigation remains responsive. Pin accepted payload and target identity before durability, prevent duplicate sends, revalidate before transport, preserve recovery and no replay. Persist rename destination before retiring source. Normal widget destruction never globally drains; graceful application shutdown may drain.
notes: Implemented and reviewed asynchronous draft load/index/rename, ordered durable submission continuations, and bounded background attachment preparation/retry reads. Accepted payloads stay pinned to their original target across navigation; stale identity, failed persistence, missing retry receipt and expired unconsented cache prevent dispatch. Tests hold storage blocked while proving event-loop progress, navigation and zero premature transport; 22 integration outcome rows pass, including native Cocoa. Composer, question, attachment and SessionsWindow suites pass on macOS and Arch. User-selected attachment import remains synchronous within the reviewed scope. Qualified source change; installed GUI not updated.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed and qualified on macOS and Linux; source changes are ready for review, without deployment.

title: Bound Activity rendering latency and defer hidden transcript layout
description: Review zerus-pta0: ActivityView::render regenerates HTML and synchronously replaces and fully lays out the whole QTextDocument after one changed reply (ActivityView.cpp:1254-1264). SessionsWindow calls setTimeline even when Activity is hidden. Release Qt offscreen synthetic approximately 1 KB replies: 100 replies take 125-126 ms per change; 250 take 297-299 ms; 500 take 587-596 ms; hidden 500-reply updates take 580 ms. Identical snapshots are below 0.2 ms. This blocks all input on the shared GUI event loop. Implement bounded/incremental visible transcript work and defer hidden rendering while keeping data current. Preserve reading anchors, selection, exact history, clear boundaries and delivery identities. Add meaningful event-loop latency qualification for changed long histories and hidden panels; average idle CPU is insufficient.
design: Prepare journal HTML, source QTextDocument layout, cloned browser text and cursor-line geometry on one low-priority job per view. Qt setDocument invalidates an ordinary prepared document, so install a public QAbstractTextDocumentLayout adapter delegating draw, hit testing and geometry to the owned immutable source document; map selections by identical text positions and preserve image cursor metrics. Keep one active job plus the latest pending input. Separate presentation epochs from content revisions so same-conversation streaming makes progress without accepting stale session, search, theme or geometry results. Hidden views defer work. Commit preserves current selection and reading anchors. Each dedicated job thread parks after preparation until its document tree is retired: Qt FreeType destroys thread-local faces on thread exit despite live layout references, and sharing a working renderer thread with GUI paint could race font-engine caches. At application shutdown, drain preparation, delete documents while font resources remain alive, then stop and join threads before Qt GUI global teardown. Validate bounded thread retirement, interaction contracts and main-thread gaps through first paint, not setter time alone.
notes: Implemented and reviewed in isolated source worktree based on d8ceeab. HTML, full layout and cursor geometry run off the GUI thread; immutable layout adapter preserves selection, links and full history. Dedicated workers park until document retirement to preserve FreeType thread-local faces, with at most two workers per view. Hidden views defer work and streaming coalesces without starvation. Native Cocoa 500-reply changed snapshots: 21-27 ms GUI gaps including first paint, 1.18-1.26 s background preparation. Activity and SessionsWindow suites pass on macOS Qt 6.11.2 and Arch Qt 6.12.0. title: Review desktop UI stalls under host load after performance fixes
description: Analyze main-thread responsiveness under general computer load, verify the installed version and remaining synchronous rendering or I/O paths, collect passive profiles and isolated synthetic measurements, and record prioritized findings. ActivityView.cpp and SessionList.cpp are byte-identical across the checkout and archive. Exact installed binary provenance is unconfirmed: its Mach-O UUID differs from the retained release build. An 8-second passive sample captures ActivityView::render -> setHtml/documentSize and whole-list/card painting on the main thread; fsync for ordinary draft edits is on the writer thread. No sustained total hang was captured. Isolated Release/Qt offscreen measurements with synthetic approximately 1 KB replies: changing one reply blocks setActivity for 125-126 ms with 100 replies, 297-299 ms with 250, and 587-596 ms with 500. Hidden Activity still costs 580 ms with 500 replies. Identical snapshots cost below 0.2 ms. With the existing write observer delaying only the draft worker 400 ms, loading an unrelated absent draft blocks the main thread 410 ms with only 0.13 ms thread CPU; a queued event does not run until return. Eight synthetic active rows at 2x scale repaint 25 times in two seconds (32 ms thread CPU); disabling activity animation produces zero paints in the same static fixture. These establish defects and avoidable work, not a complete attribution of the reported live freeze. Local diagnostic artifacts: /tmp/zerus-ui-review-harness and /tmp/zerus-ui-review-sample.txt. No application source edits, GUI/native restarts, live stress or publication.
Prioritized follow-ups: zerus-nug6 (P1 bounded Activity and hidden rendering), zerus-ts35 (P1 asynchronous draft barriers), zerus-3onx (P2 animation repaint regions). title: Investigate intermittent process history cache recovery failure during release qualification
description: Release candidate 38142162351, exact source 9b8463dddfef568925c6795d538d5cafd8266e63: Linux Rust unit test state::processes::history::tests::incremental_recovery_caches_exact_completion_and_rejects_other_conversation failed at history.rs:227. Initial recovery succeeded; the immediate cached-receipt replay returned starting instead of failed. Investigate cache/lock behavior under parallel unit tests; keep publication gated on successful exact-source qualification.
notes: Verified reproduction: a concurrent child fork inherits the raw history-lock file descriptor, so closing the parent descriptor can leave the same flock alive until the child execs/exits. Private pre-exec fork contention reproduced the exact cached-receipt assertion on attempt 6, with try_lock_exclusive returning EAGAIN. Fix history recovery to use existing lock_until(..., Instant::now()) and its explicit-unlock Guard, preserving nonblocking polling. No live processes are involved. A fresh exact-source candidate is required before publication.
close_reason: Reproduced an inherited flock descriptor during concurrent fork/pre-exec (old code failed on probe 6 with EAGAIN at cached-receipt replay). History recovery now uses the existing nonblocking lock_until guard, whose explicit unlock releases the inherited flock. Full Rust unit suite passed 256 tests; 100 private fork-contention probes passed after the fix. Final release candidate will independently qualify this source.

title: Confirm cold context before submitting native question answers

design: Astra design: Desktop and Android native question answers use an explicit cold-cache cost choice before any sending state or transport. Offer Submit with full context and default Cancel; pending questions cannot use the ordinary message clear/compact continuation because those actions invalidate the answer. Capture the exact target, run/conversation, question identity/source/tool/schema, emitted answer payload and raw saved form/draft state. Revalidate identity, availability, unchanged draft and no existing pending/submitted/uncertain delivery after consent; same-schema polling is allowed. Guard reentrant dialogs and duplicate sends. Android retains only an in-memory confirmation intent across rotation, drops it on process restart and enforces the gate centrally in ViewModel.send so inline, expanded, approval and skip paths cannot bypass it. Preserve native no-replay receipts and exact form replacement mechanics.
notes: Implemented and Astra-reviewed the desktop and Android common question-send cold-cache consent gates. Cancel preserves the complete saved form without creating delivery; consent pins exact target, question schema and raw draft. Android persistence-time expiry restores only its unchanged owned form and displays a question-local refusal. Final qualification: all 27 desktop modal scenarios; full 10 SessionsWindow shards, QuestionCard and HgsClient on Arch and Mac; Android plain Debug and Firebase Debug/Pilot each 519 tests with no failures, errors or skips, plus lint and signed/minified builds. title: Start hgs subprocesses without blocking the GUI thread
description: runHgs in tray/src/HgsClient.cpp starts about one hgs child per second (local ls every 2 s, peer ls over ssh, git-status, inspect, recovery, accounts) with QProcess on the GUI thread. On macOS Qt's vforkfd falls back to fork(), costing about 4 ms of main-thread time per launch in the large GUI process; Linux forks from the same thread.
acceptance_criteria: Launching and reaping hgs children no longer runs fork/exec on the GUI thread on macOS or Linux; timeouts, cancellation, ordering of results and error reporting stay unchanged; HgsClient tests pass.
notes: 2026-10-10: ProcessRunner owns all QProcess launches for runHgs, runWrite and requestRecovery on one worker thread (hgs-process-runner); results are queued to the owner on the GUI thread, owner destruction kills and reaps its children, a post routine reaps at exit; Linux uses UseVFork with Qt >= 6.7. GUI-thread cost per launch ~0.5 ms -> ~0.005 ms in a microbenchmark (the live profile showed ~4.2 ms fork). Residual on macOS: fork() takes malloc zone locks via atfork handlers, so a GUI allocation during a worker fork can still wait briefly; posix_spawn would avoid it. Branch perf/process-launch.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: full Qt suite passed on macOS (49/49) and Linux (48/48); in main as of b093ddb and installed on the Mac and arch on 2026-10-10.

title: Recovery jitter can exceed its 10% bound by a rounding error

For jitter 100, delay * 1.1 is not exact (90 * 1.1 = 99.00000000000001), so due_at exceeded the documented maximum and session_limits_wait_for_reset_and_interval_mode_uses_its_own_budget failed about once per 101 random job IDs (CI main for 6fd2598). title: Recovery keeps scheduling continuations while the agent is working

Recovery reached attempt 11 and kept the panel at 'Waiting to retry (N attempts, repeats until stopped)' with the 'Limit reached' chip beside a working agent. Another Claude session on the same account received 11 queued '[HGS automatic recovery]' prompts in one user turn. Expected: a provider error followed by continued agent activity in the same turn must not schedule another continuation, the panel should not claim it is waiting to retry while the agent is working, and continuations must not queue up. Related: 2e28c15 reset-aware session limit recovery.

title: Fix local file and folder opening from the file-reference dialog
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Open a local file reference in Activity on Linux/Wayland and click Open file or Open folder.

## Actual Behavior
The requested desktop application does not visibly open. The file exists, and xdg-open succeeds with the desktop application environment. Investigate the Qt dispatch path and modal-dialog lifetime without touching native agent processes.

## Acceptance Criteria
Both actions launch the expected local path reliably, failures remain visible, and the dialog preserves path safety. Cover the verified root cause with an isolated regression test.
acceptance_criteria: Open file and Open folder launch the expected local path reliably after dialog destruction. Copy path keeps local and remote dialogs open so the user can copy first and then open the file, folder or SSH terminal. Failures remain visible; regression tests use isolated synthetic paths.
notes: Queued file/folder dispatch after modal destruction fixes the Qt Wayland activation-token lifetime bug. Copy path now keeps local and remote dialogs open; tests cover copying before file, folder and SSH actions. The full Linux sessionswindow suite passed 140 tests with two existing skips, the three dialog cases passed on macOS, and the real Wayland fixture opened each requested target once. The verified GUI update is installed on both platforms.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed: copy keeps the dialog open; opening actions dispatch after its destruction. Linux, macOS and Wayland fixture checks passed.

title: Show Codex hook trust requests in Activity
description:

Cover startup without a conversation, changed prompts, review transitions and duplicate submissions with isolated tests.
close_reason: Implemented native startup hook consent in Activity, including explicit choices, scoped Review-to-Terminal navigation, stale request rejection and idempotent receipts. Rust tests, isolated tmux transport tests and the three affected Qt suites passed.

title: Quit the desktop GUI gracefully on SIGTERM and own its live update in the repository
description: hgs-tray has no SIGTERM handler, so systemctl restart/stop and launchctl unload in tray/install.sh kill it before aboutToQuit runs DraftWrites::flush; queued draft writes can be lost. Agents therefore wrote ad-hoc /tmp update scripts (tray menu Quit, staging in ~/Applications or ~/.local/bin, verification) and left .zerus-* staging folders and old bundles behind. (1) Handle SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP on Unix by calling the same quit as the tray menu; a repeated signal keeps its default action. (2) Provide one repository-owned live update for the installed GUI: unique staging beside the target removed on every outcome, graceful quit (SIGTERM when the running build supports it, otherwise the platform quit request), exactly one rollback copy in a fixed location, restart through the service manager, verification that nonempty drafts and native agent/tmux process identities are unchanged, and ~/.local/share/hgs/build-provenance.json. tray/install.sh uses it when replacing a running GUI. Follow-ups: one-time sweep of legacy .zerus-* folders and an agent protocol rule.
close_reason: Done in ea3d52d: SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP quit through the tray's Quit; tray/install.sh replaces a changed GUI via tray/update-installed.py (unique staging, graceful quit, one rollback copy, restart, draft/native/image checks, build-provenance.json). Verified live on Linux 2026-10-12: a running pre-handler GUI quit through its tray menu, 70 nonempty drafts and 17 native processes kept; the new GUI's SigCgt includes SIGTERM. macOS process/socket/image detection verified read-only.

title: durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive admits a held submission after a stale inspection
description: CI run 38248109222 (449d242, 2026-10-12) failed Arch desktop: durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive(compact-run) found a transport after the identity changed. A va-kids Windows run failed start-conversation, and local loaded runs failed send-run and start-run (4 of 160). Trace: the test injected changed-identity at 81 ms, and a fixture inspection that had read details.json before save() delivered run-one at 82 ms, so the held submission was admitted when the draft write finished.
close_reason: durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive now settles inspections after the identity change while the draft write is held: it starts its own inspection once HgsClient accepts one and waits for that reply, so no older reply can restore the previous identity. 0 failures in 192 loaded runs (4 in 160 before).

title: Design desktop and mobile voice input with host speech adapters
description: Research existing Zerus desktop/mobile/relay integration and the current GigaAM family. notes: Architecture assessment completed on 2026-10-12. Proposed boundary: host-configured speech profiles, first-party GigaAM adapter in an optional services/speech Python service, Rust hgs speech gateway, native desktop/Android recording, existing outbound relay routes for mobile. Speech host selection is independent of agent session host. Current connector requests() awaits execute() serially, so inference must use quick durable submit plus status/result/cancel operations. Current relay COMPUTER operations target the enrolled gateway; peer speech routing requires an explicit additive contract and native allowlist updates. GigaAM Multilingual 220M/600M is newer than v3; upstream does not provide a matched v3 versus Multilingual benchmark. Recommend evaluating v3_e2e_rnnt for formatted Russian dictation, v3_e2e_ctc and multilingual_large_ctc before choosing a shipped default. title: coldCacheClearKeepsDraftAndPinsIdentity loses dismiss_prompt on hosted macOS
description: CI run 38242010414 (d6655cf, 2026-10-12) failed macOS desktop: TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheClearKeepsDraftAndPinsIdentity at tray/tests/test_sessionswindow.cpp:1805, dismissPayload["dismiss_prompt"] was false (expected true). No tray source changed since the green run 38241463045 (3dc6aca), so this is a timing flake in the 'chooser dismissed with Esc' step, separate from the stale-inspection cause fixed under zerus-441j. close_reason: Root cause: fixture capture files were written non-atomically while tests waited only for existence, so a test could parse an empty clear.json (dismiss_prompt false). title: Show exact Dev build identity in desktop About and update notices
description: Owner reports that repeated patch-zero desktop versions conceal mini-updates. Verified: scripts/dev_updates.py seals desktop versionName from VERSION while keeping a separate buildNumber; Android already embeds -dev.N. Package staging verifies actual embedded identity and the sealer rejects mismatched source, dirty state or sequence. Legacy published catalogs and stable/nightly package contracts remain supported. title: Desktop reply banners fire for Kimi scheduled cron ticks and lost focus/idle gating
description: On macOS, each routine reply from a Kimi recurring cron job (CronCreate */15) posts a 'Zerus — New reply' banner. Two causes, verified 2026-10-11: (1) the zerus-vww8 idle gating and zerus-w9sm application-focus suppression were only hot-patched into installed GUI binaries and never committed; installing main 3901833 (0.41.0) on Linux and macOS removed them (installed binaries no longer import QGuiApplication::applicationState). (2) Even with idle gating, a cron-fired Kimi turn ends fully idle (activity/phase idle, no children), so every scheduled tick is a banner-eligible reply. Kimi 2.1.1 sends originKind=cron_job/cron_missed in its TurnStarted hook and journals cron.add/cron.delete in wire.jsonl; hgs drops both. Expected: re-land focus suppression and idle gating; scheduled-tick replies stay unread but do not banner while the scheduled job remains, and the final reply after the job is removed still notifies.
notes:
Follow-up 2026-10-11: owner reported the 21:30 tick still 'notified'. Notification Center showed no Zerus banner after the 21:24 Mac deploy; the remaining signal was the unread mark/badge, which the first fix intentionally kept. Now hgs does not advance reply_id for scheduled ticks while recurring_schedules > 0, and a read reply never moves back behind the read mark during skipping (transition from pre-origin journal rows).
Original implementation (55bc4e4): hgs journals Kimi TurnStarted origin_kind as turn_origin; Kimi sessions report recurring_schedules folded from wire.jsonl cron.add/cron.delete (one-shot excluded; null while unknown); AttentionTracker re-lands zerus-w9sm focus suppression and zerus-vww8 idle gating and consumes scheduled replies silently while recurring jobs remain. Validation: Rust unit tests, scripts/ci/cli.sh (63 modules, 0 failed), all 52 Qt CTest suites, installed on Linux and macOS with native identities and drafts unchanged; 21:30 tick verified reply_scheduled=true without a Notification Center banner.
close_reason: Fixed in 55bc4e4 and d8ceeab; installed on Linux and macOS. Live: the 21:30 tick reported reply_scheduled without a Notification Center banner, and after d8ceeab the 21:45 tick left reply_id on the read reply (no unread mark, badge or banner).

title: test_late_dispatch_target_cleans_after_gateway_deadline: late target process survived on Ubuntu CI
description: test_mobile_worktrees_transport.WorktreeTransport.test_late_dispatch_target_cleans_after_gateway_deadline failed once on CI (ubuntu-24.04) in run 38122605296 (b634f8a, which only changed test timing elsewhere): 'late target Git/native process survived its own mobile budget' at tests/test_mobile_worktrees_transport.py:43 after the 9 s wait; the message does not say whether the post-checkout hook or the late remote native hgs survived. First failure in the last 40 main CI runs; CLI (macos-15) passed in the same run. Determine whether the mobile budget cleanup is unreliable or the test margin is too tight.
notes: 2026-10-11 root cause: test helper, not the connector. The CI test lasted 35.2 s, so the wait loop ended early when both processes looked dead (zombies, ~t35) and the immediate re-check in assertFalse saw one as alive. Linux briefly reports state X (dead) while a parent reaps a zombie; MobilePeers.running() treated anything but Z as running. Probe on Arch (5000 reaps): Z->X->gone in 479 cases, 477 dead-then-alive flips with the old rule, 0 when X counts as dead. Locally the mobile budget kills the hook and late native hgs at ~t36 against a t39 window (24/24 loaded runs). Fix: treat X like Z in running() and the four other test zombie checks (test_process_control single-shot check, test_input/test_pause/test_mobile_worktrees_native wait loops).
close_reason: Fixed in 5eed3d3: process-state test checks treat X (dead) like Z; CLI (ubuntu-24.04) and CLI (macos-15) passed in run 38124360082, which includes it.

title: Show repository publication status on session cards
description:
## Summary
The owner wants the session card to show whether work has been pushed because local-only work has nearly been lost. Design a compact repository/branch publication indicator beside the existing project/branch line, distinguishing tracked and untracked working changes, commits ahead of the tracked remote, absent upstream and stale or unavailable remote verification. Status belongs to the actual session folder and branch and can be shared by several sessions; do not imply feature ownership or completed remote backup from a stale local ref.

## Acceptance Criteria
A reviewable design shows local changes and unpublished commits separately, with repository identity, remote/upstream and last verification in details. Synced requires adequate current evidence. Non-Git folders, worktrees, detached HEAD, divergent branches and offline machines have explicit states. No automatic commit, push, discard or cleanup. Implement after the product design is agreed.
design: The owner approved the trial on 2026-10-10. Implemented native outline diff, upload, download and cloud check/question icons beside the project/branch line. Distinct counters preserve local file changes and outgoing/incoming commits, with conflict color and exact hover details. Publication verification is read-only and separate from fleet/agent polling; local tracking refs alone never imply a verified remote. Worktrees use their own checkout identity; archives and ordinary non-Git folders have no live publication badge. See docs/reference.md for evidence, refresh, expiration and compatibility behavior.
notes:
Implemented and validated locally without committing or publishing this trial. Rust 1.85: 196 unit tests passed. Ten isolated real-Git publication contracts and 16 existing worktree contracts passed. Qt client/workspace suites passed (74 and 16 cases); integrated session-card checks passed, including shared-folder deduplication, unchanged draft/selection/focus, both themes and 280/360/500 px layouts. Desktop builds and source/privacy checks passed. Native Qt previews are in /tmp/zerus-git-status-preview.
Owner explicitly authorized commit and push on 2026-10-10. Publication is scoped to Git status badges and their read-only backend; other active work is excluded.
Owner-authorized publication completed on 2026-10-10: commit a753770 is pushed to origin/main after rebasing onto concurrent reviewed main updates. The exact integrated revision builds the desktop and passes 198 Rust 1.85 unit tests, 10 isolated Git publication contracts, all 23 worktree contracts, Qt client/workspace suites (74/16 passes including setup and cleanup), and focused integrated window checks (6 passes). Source/privacy gates pass; drafts, selection and editor focus are preserved.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified the owner-approved trial with native icons, independent bounded read-only Git evidence and Qt previews.

title: Separate session-limit recovery with reset-time and interval policies
description:
## Summary
A confirmed Claude session limit with a reset time currently enters the temporary rate-limit retry schedule. Add a distinct session_limit class with a default wait-for-reset policy and an optional per-class delay sequence using existing recovery syntax. Parse native reset evidence with its event time and timezone, preserve manual handling of permanent quota/billing/authentication failures, and expose settings and waiting status.

## Acceptance Criteria
Existing policies migrate without losing schedules. Session-limit recovery defaults to the known reset deadline, supports interval retries, and safely handles missing reset evidence. Tests cover native classification/reset extraction, policy compatibility, cancellation, class switching and settings round trips. Update reference documentation.
notes:
Implemented session_limit recovery policy v3 with default reset mode and optional independent interval schedule (300,0 fallback), native error/reset normalization, legacy episode migration, shared Qt settings and reset status. Verified 195 Rust tests on Rust 1.85, 13 isolated recovery integration tests, focused Qt recovery/settings/quota regressions (9 passes including setup/cleanup), source/privacy checks and dependency notice collection. Qt qualification used a temporary HEAD tray checkout with only this feature overlaid because existing in-progress zerus-6i4u changes have undefined Start fresh methods in the working tree. No commit, deployment or remote sync.
Owner-authorized publication completed on 2026-10-10: commit 2e28c15 is pushed to origin/main. The exact staged source tree builds hgs-tray and passes 193 Rust tests on Rust 1.85, 13 private recovery integration tests and the focused Qt recovery/settings/quota suite (9 passes including setup/cleanup), plus source/privacy checks. The lower Rust count excludes the separate in-progress Start fresh work. Unrelated working changes remain local. Repository publication indicators are tracked separately in zerus-l8v7.
close_reason: Implemented and verified reset/interval session-limit recovery, legacy policy/episode compatibility, native deadline extraction, synchronized settings and UI regressions. Working tree remains uncommitted.

title: Research anonymous Android dev distribution and update delivery

Native Android PackageInstaller supports conditional self-updates without user action on Android 12+, with install-source approval, current target API and UPDATE_PACKAGES_WITHOUT_USER_ACTION; always handle STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION. GitHub releases/latest excludes prereleases and public REST calls are limited to 60/hour per originating IP; Actions artifacts require sign-in. Obtainium and own F-Droid binary repos offer account-free client-managed updates. Appcircle public testing links support auth=None; its in-app update API is a separate Enterprise App Store feature. Diawi expiration/installation limits suit temporary handoffs. Expo EAS internal URLs permit anonymous access by default. Firebase requires tester Google sign-in; App Center distribution is retired. Current Google FAQ explicitly exempts direct sideloading from the September 2026 initial participating-store rollout; prepare for the announced 2027 expansion. Local source: pilot is nondebuggable but still uses debug signingConfig, no updater/installer permissions implemented. Public APK HEAD was HTTP 200 without credentials. Signing continuity and existing installed data must be preserved before broad distribution. Sources: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageInstaller.SessionParams ; https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/faq ; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases ; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api ; https://wiki.obtainium.imranr.dev/app_tracking/ ; https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Setup_an_F-Droid_App_Repo/ ; https://docs.appcircle.io/testing-distribution/create-or-select-a-distribution-profile ; https://docs.appcircle.io/enterprise-app-store/in-app-updates ; https://www.diawi.com/features-services ; https://docs.expo.dev/build/internal-distribution/ ; https://firebase.google.com/docs/app-distribution/get-set-up-as-a-tester?platform=android ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/appcenter/distribution/uploading . Sent' with the raw envelope. design: Require an available non-bare checkout catalog containing both the selected path and a saved project folder on the selected machine. Keep successful creation evidence in the dialog until the refreshed catalog catches up; recheck it against current project folders. Preserve project catalogs and normal folder launch behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Created and selected linked worktrees show a neutral project-worktree preview. Unrelated repositories and plain folders retain the warning. Project and machine changes cannot reuse stale membership evidence. Synthetic local and remote cases pass.
notes: Verified worktree catalogs now connect the selected folder to saved project folders on the same machine. Successful creation retains dialog-local membership until catalog refresh; unrelated, bare and unavailable folders keep the warning. Existing-picker, new-worktree, subdirectory, project-switch and machine-switch checks passed (10 worktree-panel checks on Linux and macOS), along with the full Linux GUI suites and affected macOS window scenarios. No project folders or worktrees are created implicitly.
close_reason: Both GUI corrections are implemented, tested on Linux and macOS, and installed on the development machines. Native sessions and CLI binaries were preserved.

title: Render native question replies as readable Activity answer cards
description: Codex optional-question replies appear in Activity as a raw send_user_message_question_reply envelope with JSON and transport IDs. Render recognized replies with a clear question and answer, preserving literal content and message identity. Keep unrecognized or malformed messages intact and do not change native delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Known native reply envelopes render readable question/answer cards without exposed transport markup. Escaping, unsupported input fallback and existing Activity behavior are covered by synthetic tests. Deploy and push the approved correction.
notes: Implemented readable native reply cards for journal, recorded context, local delivery and search. Question context is muted; the literal answer has its own highlighted section. Strict envelope/schema recognition preserves malformed or example input, and escaping prevents markup/resources from becoming active. Full Activity suites passed on Linux and macOS (89 tests each, one existing preview skip); synthetic light/dark previews remain outside Git. Installed both GUIs and verified build identity, running services, unchanged CLI binaries and native process identities.
close_reason: Readable answer cards were validated on Linux and macOS, deployed with native process preservation, and pushed to origin/main as 2f62568. Synthetic previews remain outside Git.

title: Refresh product README and capture synthetic feature screenshots
description:
## Summary
Replace the exhaustive README with a compact ADE presentation centered on persistent tmux sessions, multi-machine work, notifications and peer-to-peer project/config synchronization. Show supported native integrations including DeepSeek Harness as icons. Capture the real Qt UI with synthetic fixture data and keep screenshots out of commits pending owner review.

## Acceptance Criteria
Concise README with linked operational documentation, truthful support scope and mobile roadmap. Reviewable screenshots of core features contain only synthetic data. No source or tracker commit, push or remote sync.
notes:
Replaced the exhaustive README with a compact English product page, four agent icon badges including DeepSeek Harness, a mobile roadmap and four real Qt screenshots with synthetic data. Added English installation and operational reference documents, mirrored the English-language rule in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, and verified 27 local links plus desktop/narrow previews. Selected lossless WebP images total 200572 bytes; capture fixtures and originals stay outside the repository. No commits or remote sync.
After the owner approved publication, the English documentation and four reviewed screenshots were committed and pushed as 9b836f5. Publication and verified Linux/macOS deployment are tracked in zerus-3at. The current English operational reference is an edited adaptation of the original manual; capture fixtures and screenshot originals remain outside Git.
close_reason: Implemented and verified; local changes remain uncommitted for owner review.

title: Prepare public binary dependency notices and packaging
description:
## Description

Before distributing binary releases, collect licenses, copyright notices and any required source/relinking materials for the exact Qt, Chromium, KDE and Rust dependencies shipped. Verify clean installation on Linux and macOS and add repeatable build/secret-scan CI. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is a source inventory, not a completed binary distribution notice bundle.

## Acceptance Criteria

Repeatable release validation and exact shipped dependency notices are reviewed before public binary distribution.

title: Promote ordinary Codex deferred follow-ups
description:
## Summary

src/state/input_queue.rs only promotes Codex pending steers when the native UI explicitly offers Escape to interrupt and send. Ordinary deferred follow-ups remain read-only in Activity. Add verified native promotion preserving draft, attachments, order and exact queue identity. Never use generic Escape for an unsupported queue type.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.

title: Read Claude context capacity from native telemetry
description:
## Summary

Claude usage currently provides tokens without verified context-window capacity. Add a composable native statusline telemetry reader scoped to run, conversation and model, preserving existing user statusline configuration. Handle stale data, model changes and compaction. Do not infer capacity from a model name.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.

title: Change Claude model and effort from Activity
description:
## Summary

src/state/effort.rs directs Claude model and effort changes to Terminal. Add verified per-session native controls with capability checks, preserving account defaults and drafts. Cover Linux and macOS behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.

title: Support native DeepSeek context reset when available
description:
## Summary

Clear context is intentionally disabled for DeepSeek because the integrated native SessionController has no supported reset method. Add a capability-gated native reset when the upstream interface supports it. Preserve conversation identity and never truncate provider-owned history or replace a running agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.

title: Avoid executing custom launchers during capability detection
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run the custom-launcher cases in tests/test_pause.py.

## Actual Behavior

The Codex capability probe in src/state/lifecycle.rs invokes the configured executable with --help before a supervised run exists. Custom launchers may block, exit, or produce side effects before run identity is recorded. Detect capabilities without executing a user wrapper outside supervision. Cover failed, cancelled and requested-conversation startup in tests/test_pause.py.

## Expected Behavior

Launchers run only inside supervision and failures retain the intended run identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Regression tests reproduce the original condition and pass reliably after a verified fix, without bypassing identity checks or relying on another account.

title: Sweep legacy desktop staging folders and require the repository live update for agents
description: Follow-up to zerus-scsy. (3) Earlier ad-hoc updates left hidden .zerus-* staging folders and old hgs-tray.app copies in ~/Applications and ~/.local/bin; let the live update remove only known legacy patterns that are empty folders or GUI copies no process runs, after unregistering bundles from LaunchServices. (4) Add an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule: update local installations only with install.sh, tray/install.sh and mac-install.sh (live GUI replacement through tray/update-installed.py) and never stage GUI copies by hand.

title: macOS recovery LaunchAgent respawns every 10 s while a detached worker holds the lock
description: Observed 2026-10-12 on a Mac: com.hgdev.hgs-recovery showed no PID and 'spawn scheduled' with over 1,800 runs, each exiting 0, while an 'hgs recovery worker' started by ensure_worker() (setsid, parent launchd) held recovery/worker.lock. worker() returns 0 when the lock is taken, and KeepAlive=true with ThrottleInterval=10 relaunches it indefinitely. Recovery itself works, but the managed job never owns the worker and wastes a process spawn every 10 s. The race appears after a service restart (kickstart -k) when any hgs invocation spawns a detached worker first. Consider waiting for the lock in the managed worker, having a detached worker yield to the service, or KeepAlive on unsuccessful exit only. Check whether Linux systemd (Restart policy) can loop the same way.

title: Kimi: an unchanged model/effort request is reported as not confirmed and blocks later input
description: hgs settings with the model and effort a Kimi 2.1.1 session already uses sends /model; Kimi answers 'Already using <model> with thinking off.', hgs reports 'settings change not confirmed', and later compact/clear refuse with 'previous input has not been confirmed by the agent' until Terminal is checked. Found with a keyless single-model fixture; the desktop picker normally sends only a changed selection. Reject an unchanged request before typing, or accept the native 'Already using' confirmation.
close_reason: Fixed in 358e241: Kimi 2.1 status lines are read by matching the session model's slot (display name with overrides), so an unchanged request is confirmed without typing and real model/effort changes are confirmed; the model picker walk handles the non-wrapping 2.1 list. Verified on real Kimi 2.1.1.

title: Updates page links to a README anchor that no longer exists
description: tray/src/UpdatesWidget.h opens https://github.com/ufna/zerus#installation, but README.md has no Installation heading (installation moved to docs/installation.md). Pre-existing at c7bc2be; found during the Windows Phase 1 review. Point the button at docs/installation.md (or a per-platform anchor such as #windows for portable builds).

title: Keep terminal-read question panels literal on Android
description: Android QuestionUi renders every non-approval prompt, body and option description as Markdown, including trust_request cards and panels read from a terminal (claude/codex/kimi folder trust, claude_resume, codex_update, claude_terminal_choice). Their text is already rendered terminal output; a folder path containing Markdown characters such as * _ \ or [..](..) can display altered in a trust decision. Desktop (zerus-rxzz) renders Markdown only for agent-authored sources (hook, codex_async, kimi_wire, dsh_native, claude_native_question) and keeps approval/trust flags literal. Align Android with that rule and update docs/mobile-architecture.md.

title: Mac tray installer reuses a CMake cache with SDK paths removed by an Xcode update
description: Verified 2026-10-11: ~/.local/src/hgs/tray/build kept CMake cache entries for MacOSX26.0.sdk (for example the Cups library) after Xcode moved to MacOSX27.0.sdk. Configuring then fails because Qt6::WebEngineWidgets interface include paths point at the missing SDK, so mac-install.sh cannot install the GUI. Moving the build directory aside fixed it. tray/install.sh should detect a cached SDK path that no longer exists and reconfigure from a clean cache.
notes: Fixed: tray/install.sh clears build/CMakeCache.txt and build/CMakeFiles before configuring when any cached SDK path is gone; bracketed FIND_PACKAGE details are parsed per path. Verified against the real Mac caches (stale MacOSX26.0 cache detected; current 27.0 caches kept). tests/test_mac_install.py TrayInstallCache runs the macOS branch with fake tools.
close_reason: Fixed in ad263e8. Detection verified on the real Mac caches (removed MacOSX26.0 SDK flagged, current MacOSX27.0 caches kept); mac-install.sh completed with the current cache.

title: macOS swarm installer can unload the worker when its plist changes during a restart
description: Verified 2026-10-11 during mac-install.sh mac: install-swarm-service.py rewrote com.hgdev.hgs-swarm.plist (PATH differs under SSH), ran launchctl bootout, then launchctl print still found the service while it was being removed, so the --restart branch ran launchctl kickstart -k and failed with exit 113. The install aborted after the CLI step and the swarm LaunchAgent stayed unloaded until a rerun bootstrapped it. Wait for bootout to complete (or bootstrap after a changed plist) instead of kickstarting a service being removed.
notes: Fixed: scripts/launchd_agent.py waits (bounded, 15 s) for launchctl print to fail after bootout of a changed definition, then bootstraps; kickstart runs only for an unchanged loaded agent and reports failures. Swarm and recovery installers share it; caller PATH is split so duplicate directories collapse. tests/test_launchd_agent.py fakes the asynchronous removal observed on macOS.
close_reason: Fixed in ad263e8. Verified on the Mac: mac-install.sh reloaded the changed swarm and recovery definitions through bootout, wait and bootstrap without a kickstart race; both workers run and native processes were unchanged.

title: Android: dismiss a Claude chooser before clearing context
description: Follow-up to zerus-4p2s. Desktop and hgs clear-context accept an explicit dismiss_prompt request when inspect reports clear_context_dismiss (Claude waits in an approval, question or other chooser). Android ContextUi and the mobile connector still pass only the fixed clear-context fields; add the same separate Dismiss and clear confirmation and allow the reviewed optional field end to end without breaking API v1.

title: Flaky processes history recovery test under full parallel suite
description: state::processes::history::tests::incremental_recovery_caches_exact_completion_and_rejects_other_conversation failed once in a full local cargo test --locked run on macOS (2026-10-11): assertion at src/state/processes/history.rs:227, job status was not "failed" after appending ~9 MiB of padding. Three isolated reruns and three further full runs passed. Likely timing/size dependence of the incremental recovery window under parallel load; find the exact cause before changing limits.
close_reason: Duplicate of zerus-j2lv: c7bc2be releases process-history locks explicitly; a concurrent fork could inherit the close-only flock.

title: Report last seen time for offline peer routes
description: Offline direct peers now appear in Android Machines from a last verified identity (zerus-40fr), but the relay clears a peer route's last_seen when it goes offline, so peers show plain Offline. Keep the last successful peer heartbeat time for offline routes in both the Rust relay and the Python reference so Android can show Offline / last seen.

title: Fix marker race in mobile worktree native hook test
description: test_mobile_worktrees_native.await_hook waits only for hook.pid to exist, but the post-checkout hook creates it with open(...,'w') before writing the PID; a read in between raises ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''. Seen once in a full local cli.sh run on 2026-10-11 (macOS); 3/3 isolated reruns passed. Wait for non-empty content or write atomically via rename.

title: Add Git publication status badges to Android session cards
description: Desktop cards show changed files, outgoing/incoming commits and verified-sync marks from a separate bounded git status read. Android snapshots carry only branch/worktree metadata. Adding the badges needs an additive read-only relay and connector operation with freshness/verification semantics matching GitStatusBadge; coordinate relay rollout and keep API v1 compatible.

title: Raise the macOS desktop minimum to 14.0
description: Homebrew Qt 6.11 qtbase/qtwebengine frameworks are built for macOS 14.0 while tray/CMakeLists.txt declared 12.0, so the app could never start below 14 and ld warned. Raise CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to 14.0 (also lifting stale cached values), declare LSMinimumSystemVersion in Info.plist and document the requirement. QtQml/QtQuick/QtPositioning/QtWebChannel bottles target the bottle host OS; those ld warnings are a Homebrew packaging artifact.
close_reason: LSMinimumSystemVersion and the deployment target are 14.0; cached 12.0 build dirs are raised; macosbundle and all 54 GUI tests pass.

title: Android: treat a capabilities 404 as presence_alerts absent
description: Alert-only mode keeps its last known state when GET /v1/capabilities fails with anything but 401/403. A proxy or relay answering 404/5xx persistently would keep a stale alerts-on mode. Treat 404 as feature-absent; consider bounding stale mode for repeated 5xx/network failures.

title: Relay alerts: run candidate expiry in its own transaction
description: Expiry of alert candidates shares the maintenance transaction with planning and delivery; a persistent failure in any selected workspace would stop expiry (the 24 h storage bound) everywhere. Split expiry into its own short elected transaction when the pass is next touched.

title: Relay alerts: bound the maintenance pass's global event lock window
description: When any plan delivers, the elected maintenance pass keeps the global event row locked while applying all plans (up to 32 workspaces x 1000 candidate statements plus expired drops); heartbeats with events queue behind it under lock_timeout 5s. Apply drop/wait-only plans without event locks or bound rows per pass before multi-tenant growth.

title: Relay alerts: prefer the local route when a computer reports through several routes
description: A heartbeat on a lagging route can resolve or keep alert candidates for a computer reachable through two gateways (candidates.rs resolution reads that route's snapshot). Prefer the local route, as the registry already does. Self-heals when the lagging route reports; a miss needs a multi-gateway topology and the route to stop within one poll interval.

title: Phase 1 shared-read hardening follow-ups
description: Parked from the Phase 1 final review (branch worktree-presence-notifications, commits cd72e02..ce4d86b): (1) AttentionTracker tombstones key main requests by attentionId without attention_started, so a back-to-back identity-less request can get no desktop banner in a narrow window; (2) attention_started is mixed into the signature even with a unique attention_id, so repeated PermissionRequest/PostCompact can change it once; (3) codex_questions oversized-line branch skips the listing deadline check for runs of >1 MiB lines; (4) phone treats a completed-but-unapplied attention mark as sent; desktop marks with an unknown signature retry and spend the indexing budget; (5) DeepSeek renames lose name-keyed marks; ReadMarkSync per-host fairness; per-write cost of hgs read; test gaps listed in the Phase 1 ledger.

title: macOS swarm worker survives install-time kickstart -k
description: 2026-10-11 on the owner's Mac: after ./install.sh replaced ~/.local/bin/hgs (01:29), com.hgdev.hgs-swarm still ran PID 14560 started 2026-10-10 14:01 (launchctl print: runs = 2, last terminating signal = Terminated: 15), while the recovery worker restarted. scripts/install-swarm-service.py runs launchctl kickstart -k with check=True and install succeeded, so the worker likely ignores or outlives the restart and keeps running an older binary. Determine whether this is intended and make updates take effect.

title: Windows support: start from the approved design
description: Entry point for Windows support. The owner approved a phased direction on 2026-10-10: Phase 1 makes Windows a control console (native Qt GUI and a client subset of the same hgs binary managing remote Linux/macOS machines over the system OpenSSH client); Phase 2 adds a native Windows session host behind a terminal-backend abstraction, following the persistent ConPTY-daemon model used by Orca. Nothing is implemented yet. The design records verified starting facts (the Windows compile-error map, GUI portability gaps, CI budget) and an ordered list of first steps.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1: hgs.exe and hgs-tray.exe build and test on Windows, manage remote machines over ssh.exe, and the nightly publishes a verified portable zip. Phase 2 receives its own spec before implementation. Linux and macOS behavior and compatibility remain unchanged.
notes: Phase 1 implemented in an uncommitted worktree (2026-10-12) and verified on a Windows 11 PC and Linux; pending owner review and commit. Follow-ups: interactive-desktop checks and pre-nightly owner actions. Phase 2 needs its own spec before implementation. Keep host access details in private infrastructure configuration, never in Git or Beads.

title: test_body_cap_nonfinite_and_poll_bounds flakes against the Rust relay with Broken pipe
description: Found 2026-10-10 during zerus-rk5b.1 Task 4: services/mobile/tests/test_rust_relay.py running RelayTests.test_body_cap_nonfinite_and_poll_bounds (test_relay.py:239) intermittently fails with aiohttp ClientOSError [Errno 32] Broken pipe. The client POSTs a body just over 1 MiB to /v1/node/heartbeat; the relay answers 413 and closes the socket before the client finishes sending. Reproduced on base d34a9f0 binary (1/30 runs), so pre-existing. Make the test tolerate an early close (accept the 413 response or the broken pipe as rejection) or have the relay drain bounded excess before closing.

title: ManagedProfileMcp codex test temp-dir cleanup races on macOS CI
description: CI run 38059066794 (4b8fa5d, 2026-10-10) failed CLI macos-15: test_account_mcp.ManagedProfileMcp.test_codex_profile_receives_native_servers_but_not_native_settings errored in TemporaryDirectory cleanup with OSError Errno 66 'Directory not empty' for zerus-mcp-*. Something still writes into the fixture directory during teardown (likely a child process). Wait for owned children or ignore late files before rmtree; the commit under test did not touch the CLI.

title: Avoid the missing Monospace font family lookup on macOS
description: hgs-tray logs 'Populating font family aliases took 52-72 ms. Replace uses of missing font family "Monospace"' once per process on macOS, a main-thread stall on first use. Candidates: the generic 'monospace' family in ActivityView process details (HTML style) and QuestionCard approval details (QFont::setFamily), and possibly Qt's default family for HTML code/pre. MarkdownHtml::monospaceFamily() already resolves an installed family.
acceptance_criteria: No 'missing font family' alias population is logged on macOS when Activity, process details and approval questions render; Linux keeps an equivalent monospace font.
close_reason: Fixed in 90248e6: Activity tool details and approval commands use the first installed family of the GitHub monospace stack (Menlo on this Mac) instead of generic monospace, which triggered a 52-72 ms font alias population and rendered in the proportional system font. Full Qt suites passed on macOS and Linux.

title: Avoid fork() malloc-lock stalls when launching hgs on macOS
description: After zerus-ilix.5, hgs children start on the ProcessRunner worker thread, but on macOS Qt's vforkfd falls back to fork(), whose atfork handlers (_malloc_fork_prepare/_malloc_fork_parent) hold every malloc zone lock for the duration of the fork (~4 ms in the large GUI process per the 2026-10-10 profile). A GUI-thread allocation during that window still waits. Options: posix_spawn-based launching on macOS inside ProcessRunner, or fewer launches through a long-lived hgs stream for local polls.
acceptance_criteria: A profile of the live macOS app shows no GUI-thread waits on malloc locks caused by hgs launches; Linux behavior is unchanged or improved; process I/O, timeouts, environment and cancellation semantics stay identical.
notes: 2026-10-10 experiments (macOS 27, M1 Pro, 40k-region process): fork 12.5-15 ms vs posix_spawn 0.27-0.30 ms per launch, but concurrent malloc (mixed sizes) and mmap+page-fault+munmap in another thread showed no stalls with either (worst <1 ms both). GUI-thread waits from worker forks are not reproducible; the remaining benefit is fork CPU (~4 ms per launch in the live GUI, ~0.4% of a core). Owner decision: implement the macOS posix_spawn backend anyway, alongside reducing hgs ls poll cost.
close_reason: macOS ProcessRunner starts children with posix_spawn (6140fdb): ~7.5 ms -> ~0.2 ms CPU per launch in a large process; live GUI worker 30 s: fork 116 ms -> posix_spawn 17 ms. GUI-thread stalls from worker forks were not reproducible. Full suites passed on macOS and Linux; installed on the Mac.

title: markdownobjects timing assertion is flaky under load
description: tray/tests markdownobjects failed once at 118 ms against a 100 ms limit while parallel builds loaded the Mac, then passed on retry. A wall-clock bound in a unit test is sensitive to CI and developer machine load. Found while implementing zerus-ilix.1.
acceptance_criteria: The test still detects pathological slowdowns without failing under ordinary parallel load on macOS and Linux.
notes: 2026-10-10: Reproduced 8/8 failures with 16 busy loops on a 10-core Mac (143-282 ms vs 100 ms). Now best-of-three thread CPU time bounded at 200 ms: culled frames ~50 ms, painting every chip ~810 ms. 35/35 passed under the same load. Branch fix/markdown-timing.
close_reason: Fixed in 267a013: best-of-three thread CPU time bounded at 200 ms; 35/35 passed under heavy load.

title: coldCacheClearKeepsDraftAndPinsIdentity fails when run alone
description: tray/tests/test_sessionswindow.cpp coldCacheClearKeepsDraftAndPinsIdentity consistently fails when run as a single test function on main (2053f52) but passes inside the full ctest shard, so it depends on state left by earlier test functions. Found while implementing zerus-ilix.1.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes alone and in its shard without relying on earlier test functions.
close_reason: Fixed in 67ddb23: details.json is written atomically before selection; 0/40 failures alone on macOS, 0/10 on Linux.

title: Limit the attention logo animation frame rate
description: SwarmButton (tray/src/SwarmButton.h) redraws at the display refresh rate (up to 120 Hz) for 1.4 s of every 3 s whenever any session needs attention, which is almost always; each frame repaints and flushes the window backing store and keeps the app awake.
acceptance_criteria: The animation runs at a bounded lower frame rate with the same visual motion, stops while the window is hidden or minimized and honors reduced motion; tests cover the timer interval.
notes: 2026-10-10: SwarmButton animates at 30 fps (kFrameMs 33) instead of the display rate, skips frames while its window is not exposed, and ignores unchanged setAppearance calls. Tests test_swarmbutton. Branch perf/swarm-animation.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: full Qt suite passed on macOS (49/49) and Linux (48/48); in main as of b093ddb and installed on the Mac and arch on 2026-10-10.

title: Explain the Android QA emulator memory-limit notification
description: Diagnose the desktop OOM notification for the merged-accounts Android QA emulator using service settings and kernel logs. Distinguish a test cgroup limit from host-wide memory exhaustion and verify the replacement test service without changing neighboring work.
close_reason: Verified cgroup OOM: the software-rendered Android QA emulator reached an explicit 3 GiB systemd MemoryMax. Guest RAM and the whole emulator/renderer cgroup budget differ. The replacement test uses 2 GiB guest RAM and a 6 GiB service limit and is running. No neighboring services or source files were changed.

title: Configure GitHub repository discovery topics
description: Add accurate GitHub topics for the shared multi-machine AI agent workspace, P2P connectivity and supported coding agents; verify the repository settings after updating.
notes: Owner requested a neater topic block like Orca. Use short ecosystem tags ade, agent-ide, orchestration and devtools; remove duplicate agent category tags while retaining multi-machine, P2P and the four actual integrations.
close_reason: Verified the compact topic set: ade, agent-ide, ai-agents, claude-code, codex, deepseek, desktop-app, devtools, kimi-code, multi-machine, orchestration, p2p, ssh, terminal, tmux.

title: Clear stale revoked-workspace read banner after disconnect and re-pair
description: Synthetic emulator reproduction on Android0.1.9: disconnect a paired fixture workspace, immediately open a new invitation for the same isolated workspace and pair again. The new credential discovers its online machine and fresh activity shows Connected/Ready, but an old catalog read can leave the previous workspace Unauthorized banner visible. Clear only obsolete connection-owned read errors; preserve unrelated mutation/storage errors. Frozen0.1.9 was not modified.

title: Remove README screenshot data caption
description: Remove the footer sentence about screenshots showing the real interface with synthetic projects, machines and messages, as requested by the owner.
close_reason: Removed the screenshot data caption from README; git diff --check passed.

title: Reconcile missing or stale team task records with Dolt history
description: The tracked passive export contains closed zerus-lzp (parallel test suites), absent from the authoritative embedded Dolt store and its pulled remote. It also contains a newer closed zerus-5bm record, while Dolt retains an older open copy. Preserve these exact export rows. Recover the records from the originating peer or database history without replacing/importing the database from JSONL; then regenerate the passive export.
notes: 2026-10-10 consolidation: zerus-a60x and zerus-t84i were verified closed in the originating peer canonical Dolt store and reconstructed in the shared authoritative store via explicit bd create/close. No JSONL import or database replacement. The peer had no Dolt remote; after configuring the project remote, normal pull reports no common ancestor. Preserve its independent database; a separate history reconciliation remains necessary.

title: Add a New session button to the Sessions panel header
description: Add a + action next to the collapse toggle and actions menu in the Sessions panel header. It opens New session for the selected machine/project, like the rail button, and hides in the collapsed strip.
close_reason: Fixed with regression tests; full Qt suite passed; GUI reinstalled and restarted (agents untouched).

title: Show Claude subagent tool approvals in Activity
description: questions::observe ignores PermissionRequest events with an agent_id, so a subagent's native approval panel gets no Activity card. Route the request to the visible panel and clear it on that agent's PostToolUse/Stop without confusing it with the main agent's request.

title: Stabilize test_living_unconfirmed_wrapper_is_not_replaced
description: tests/test_pause.py FailedStartup.test_living_unconfirmed_wrapper_is_not_replaced intermittently fails: the binding captured as 'before' after ready.exists still gets a later write that changes pid and updated (~25 ms apart). Reproduced on a clean HEAD build (4d8455d) as well as with local changes, about half of the runs under load. Wait for the supervisor's final pid before taking the snapshot, or compare only the fields the test protects.

title: Stabilize account-loading test under parallel GUI test load
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run GUI tests with ctest --test-dir tray/build -j 4.

## Actual Behavior

During the clean-repository validation, accountspage::initialLoadingPublishesOnlyGroupedAccounts timed out at the first four local rows under ctest -j 4. The isolated case and the predecessor full account suite pass; AccountsPage production source is unchanged. Investigate the fake inspect process barriers and deadlines so the test reliably exercises incremental local-first loading under parallel load without hiding product failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

The account-loading test reliably verifies incremental local-first loading under parallel test load and continues to detect real grouping regressions.

title: Expose supported DeepSeek fork, history and scheduling operations
description:
## Summary

The native DeepSeek integration leaves fork, global history search and schedule management in Native UI. Evaluate supported native APIs and expose useful operations in Zerus while preserving account/conversation identity and native engine ownership. See design/deepseek-harness/index.html.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.

title: Keep managed recovery worker ownership when clients refresh policy
description: Verified live Linux recovery runs in a detached hgs process while the user service repeatedly exits because its executor lock is held. Policy reads unconditionally spawn a detached fallback, allowing it to beat the supervisor during CLI replacement. Prefer starting an existing configured user service without restarting a healthy worker; retain the detached fallback for installations without an available user manager. Preserve delivery ownership and active native agents.
